title: Attribute-based Conditional Access Reconciler for Retention Compliance
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
Redwood needs an automated reconciliation layer that ensures accounts and sessions subject to residency and retention constraints are: 1) provisioned and deprovisioned via SCIM with residency attributes, 2) have SSO/SAML assertions annotated with retention tags at session-creation time, and 3) produce auditable justification records for periodic access reviews. Today we have fragmented signals across SCIM deltas, token metadata, and ad-hoc audit exports which causes gaps in compliance evidence and manual work for security/compliance teams.

Objective:
Build an Attribute-based Conditional Access Reconciler (ABCAR) that: (a) consumes SCIM change streams and SSO assertion events, (b) evaluates per-tenant residency + retention policies via a lightweight policy engine, (c) mutates identity attributes (SCIM) or session metadata (session tokens) when policy requires, (d) runs periodic reconciliation and generates signed proof bundles exported to the compliance evidence store. The system must support incremental rollout, be auditable, and minimize impact on login latency and provisioning throughput.

High-level approach / components:
- SCIM Delta Ingestor: consume SCIM events (full + incremental) from connectors and normalize into canonical identity records. Operates as a streaming job with idempotent checkpoints.
- Assertion Enricher: attach residency/retention attributes to SAML/OIDC session assertions when a user signs in (prefer enrichment in-identity provider hook or proxy layer). Add short-lived signed token metadata for retention classification.
- Policy Engine: attribute-based policy (ABAC) with tenant, role, data residency, and retention horizon inputs. Implement a conservative default deny for residency mismatch. Policies authored as JSON rules stored in Config Service.
- Reconciler (periodic): reconcile canonical identity state vs policies every 24h (configurable), escalate discrepancies (e.g., user with region=EU accessing US-only resources). Produce a reconciliation report and a signed proof bundle containing diffs and justification records.
- Evidence Exporter: pack signed proofs into the compliance evidence store (S3/GCS) with immutable retention TTL and KMS envelope encryption. Provide an export manifest that ties to ticket IDs, reviewer IDs, and the periodic access review run.
- Rollout & Opt-outs: allow per-tenant opt-out by explicit contract flag (enterprise-only). Provide a dry-run mode that reports potential changes without mutating SCIM or sessions.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Where to annotate: We evaluated annotating the identity record (SCIM) vs annotating session tokens. Decision: annotate both where feasible — SCIM for long-lived entitlement corrections and session metadata for runtime enforcement. This doubles writes but simplifies audits.
- Real-time vs batch: Real-time enforcement (at sign-in) is necessary to stop policy-violating sessions; but full reconciliation is batched to avoid amplifying SCIM provider rate limits.
- Consistency model: eventual consistency is acceptable for reconciliations and evidence creation, but sign-in enforcement must be strongly consistent for residency checks.
- Data retention of proofs: evidence must be immutable for the configured retention window. Proof bundles will be write-once objects encrypted with customer-shared KMS keys for Private deployments.

Acceptance criteria:
- The reconciler ingests SCIM deltas and SSO assertions and produces normalized identity records for >99.9% of events in the pipeline within 30s under normal load.
- On dry-run, the system produces a reconciliation report for a test tenant that surfaces residency mismatches and expected SCIM mutations.
- For a staged canary (10% of sign-ins), assertion enrichment adds retention/residency metadata without increasing median sign-in latency by more than 60ms.
- Proof bundles generated by a reconciliation run contain signed diffs, reviewer-ids, and timestamps and are exported to evidence S3 with successful MD5/SHA256 manifest verification.
- Admin console shows reconciliation status per tenant, counts of mismatches, and an export history with links to bundles.

Tasks (top-level):
- Integrate SCIM Delta Ingestor with existing connector framework and idempotent checkpointing.
- Implement assertion enricher as a middleware hook in the sign-in path; fall back to token-exchange annotator.
- Build policy engine library and a policy authoring UI (PM/Console).
- Implement periodic reconciliation worker, diff generator, and signed proof bundle format.
- Wire evidence exporter to compliance S3 bucket with KMS envelope encryption and immutable retention flags.
- Create admin console widgets (reconciler status, mismatch lists, export history).
- Add e2e tests and load tests (SCIM delta storm, sign-in canary).

Notes / non-goals:
- This ticket does not change tenant-level data residency enforcement for non-auth flows (e.g., data-plane workloads). That's follow-up work.
- On-prem/air-gapped deployments will surface different KMS/encryption integration; separate ticket will cover packaging.

Metrics to monitor:
- SCIM delta ingestion lag (P50/P95), reconciliation run duration, ratio of mismatches per tenant, canary sign-in latency delta, proof export success rate, and evidence-store retention TTL violations.

- Compliance export format (spec): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abcar-spec
